guides.title: API overview
guides.description: Build a master for one Debian agent, one Xray runtime and one control connection.
guides.body:
## One connection. Every control.
X-Node is a Debian 13 binary agent with one embedded Xray runtime and multiple tagged inbounds. The production master is a separate application. This reference describes the contract that master implements.

Control messages, user synchronization, telemetry and utility commands share one authenticated WebSocket. Certificate providers, artifact downloads and test transfers use their respective network protocols.

## Integration path
1. Accept an authenticated WSS connection using the `x-node.v1` subprotocol.
2. Read `agent.hello`, then respond to `state.request` with an authoritative `state.sync`.
3. Persist monotonic revisions and distinguish `state.accepted` from `state.applied`.
4. Deduplicate `traffic.report` batch IDs before billing and acknowledge durable receipt.
5. Replace online telemetry snapshots, issue user controls and request IP details only when needed.

## At a glance
| Property | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Wire format | UTF-8 JSON, protocol version `1` |
| Control transport | WSS with Bearer authentication |
| Socket subprotocol | `x-node.v1` |
| State authority | Master snapshots and revisioned deltas |
| Machine metrics | One-second sample / five-second report defaults |
| Active user IPs | Omitted by default; explicitly requested |
| Traffic accounting | Durable acknowledged batches |
| Local configuration | Connection URL and token only |

## Explore the contract
[Connect an agent](#/connection) · [State synchronization](#/synchronization) · [Command lifecycle](#/command-lifecycle) · [Remote configuration](#/configuration) · [Schemas & downloads](#/schemas)

Use the left navigation to open a message or command. Each entry includes its direction, behavior and example JSON. The downloadable schema is the machine-readable source for payload shape.

guides.title: Connection & authentication
guides.description: WSS upgrade, credentials, agent identity and reconnect behavior.
guides.body:
## WebSocket upgrade
The agent initiates a WebSocket connection to the bootstrap URL supplied by the operator. `/v1/agents/connect` is the documented master endpoint. Agent connections require WSS, including local fixtures.

```http
GET /v1/agents/connect HTTP/1.1
Host: master.example.com
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Authorization: Bearer <agent-token>
Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: x-node.v1
```

| Response | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `101` | Upgrade accepted; begin the message exchange |
| `401` | Missing or invalid Bearer credential |
| `426` | A WebSocket upgrade is required |

The master validates enrollment and authorization. Keep credentials out of query strings, redirect URLs, traces and diagnostics. The agent redacts tokens, passwords and private keys before logging.

## Envelope
```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "type": "users.delta",
  "id": "users-42",
  "revision": 42,
  "base_revision": 41,
  "data": {"upsert": [], "remove": [7]}
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `v` | Required protocol version: `1` |
| `type` | Required message name; maximum 64 characters |
| `id` | Correlation or command ID; maximum 128 characters |
| `revision` | Monotonic state revision for state mutations |
| `base_revision` | Current authorization revision expected by an incremental mutation |
| `data` | Message-specific typed JSON payload |

The maximum accepted frame is 16 MiB. Unknown envelope fields and malformed payloads are rejected. Send JSON arrays explicitly: missing or null `users` never means an empty authoritative set.

## Identity and liveness
The first application frame on a new connection is `agent.hello`. It carries a durable agent ID and a fresh process boot ID. Preserve the state directory across upgrades so that identity and unacknowledged traffic remain stable.

WebSocket Ping/Pong frames monitor transport liveness. Runtime readiness and synchronization are separate application status fields. A connected agent can still be applying configuration.

## Reconnects
Reconnect uses bounded exponential backoff. The agent requests a full snapshot after reconnect, a revision gap or receive-buffer overflow. During a master outage it uses the last accepted private state, including admission blocks. A first boot without accepted state waits for an authoritative snapshot.

guides.title: State synchronization
guides.description: Authoritative snapshots, exact base revisions and safe revocation.
guides.body:
## Full snapshot
`state.sync` establishes an authoritative baseline. It includes native `xray` configuration and an explicit `users` array. `users: []` removes every authorized user and closes revoked sessions.

## Incremental changes
After a successful snapshot, send `config.apply`, `users.sync`, `users.delta` or `user.controls` with a new `revision` and the current `base_revision`. The agent serializes application. A stale revision produces an error; a missing base or revision gap requests a new snapshot.

| Message | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `state.sync` | Full configuration and authorization baseline |
| `config.apply` | Complete configuration replacement |
| `users.sync` | Complete user-set replacement |
| `users.delta` | User additions, replacements and removals |
| `user.controls` | Admission blocks without changing credentials |

A repeated full snapshot at the successfully applied revision is acknowledged without repeating the change. Corrected configuration must use a higher revision.

## Accepted versus applied
`state.accepted` means the new authorization state has been persisted. `state.applied` means the proxy runtime has activated the configuration. `state.failed` reports an activation failure. Track both persisted authorization and runtime revision in the master.

Revocation is authoritative even if an unrelated runtime update fails. Removed users, rotated credentials and removed inbound eligibility never regain access through rollback. Old multiplexed transports carry a generation-bound identity and cannot create new leaf streams after revocation.

## Native runtime updates
The agent validates native Xray configuration before changing listeners. Compatible user-only changes use runtime managers; listener and global changes may require controlled reconstruction and close affected sessions. Keep inbound tags stable and define managed accounts in the separate user set.

guides.title: Command lifecycle
guides.description: Accepted jobs, progress, results, cancellation and deduplication.
guides.body:
## Submit a typed command
```json
{"v":1,"type":"command","id":"list-001","data":{"name":"connections.list","args":{"limit":100}}}
```

The agent emits `command.accepted`, optional `command.progress`, then `command.result`. Match the operation using the request ID. Progress data is command-specific. Results contain `id`, `command`, `status`, completion time and optional `data` or `error`.

## Concurrency and retries
Two utility workers execute jobs concurrently. The agent retains the last 128 completed results across restarts for request-ID deduplication. Use unique IDs beyond that bounded retention window; retry an uncertain operation using the same ID while it remains retained.

`jobs.list` returns the current retained job view. A result indicating that runtime reconstruction was queued is not proof that the new runtime is ready; also observe telemetry and state activation.

## Cancellation
```json
{"v":1,"type":"command.cancel","data":{"id":"list-001"}}
```

Cancellation propagates through the command context. It cannot reverse a DNS-provider mutation that has already succeeded, a committed firewall transaction or an installed release. Query retained results before deciding whether to retry.

## Host safety
Privileged actions use typed argument structures. Firewall changes include an independent rollback watchdog and require confirmation from the master after connectivity testing. Update installation requires authenticated release artifacts. Speedtests use an isolated Xray client with bounded transfers and cancellation.

## Acceptance and recovery
Bound acceptance to 30 seconds independently of protocol-defined execution deadlines. Distinguish undelivered, rejected, failed and uncertain results. Reload completion follows activation on activation_commands_v1 agents. Use update.status after reconnect; retained transaction plus current revision readiness confirms upgrade completion.

guides.title: Users, IPs & admission
guides.description: Privacy-aware active-IP reporting and precise user/IP controls.
guides.body:
## User identity and limits
Each user has a positive numeric `id`, credentials, eligible `inbound_tags` and optional per-agent quotas. `active_ip_limit` counts distinct current source IPs; `connection_limit` counts authenticated logical TCP streams and UDP associations across every eligible inbound. Zero quotas are unlimited.

`speed_limit_mbps` is the normal rate and `burst_speed_limit_mbps` is the always enforced ceiling. After `speed_limit_after_seconds` consecutive seconds above normal (default 10), the normal cap applies. Traffic below 90% of normal for `speed_limit_reset_seconds` (default 1) restores bursts. Upload/download and all inbounds share this policy. `users.speed` reports its active rate. `block_new` prevents new admission while preserving established eligible streams. Master decisions implement approximate global totals; the agent does not request a master reservation for every stream.

## Active IPs are requested data
By default, routine user telemetry omits source IP addresses. Set `telemetry.include_active_ips: true` in accepted configuration to request active IPs in recurring reports, or issue `users.active_ips` for a one-time query. Every reported IP is associated with its `user_id`; an IP without an active stream is not an online observation.

Session details returned by an explicit `connections.list` query include their source IP and user identity. Turning recurring reporting off does not prevent the master from making an explicit detail request.

## Drop or temporarily block an IP
Use `ips.control` with a literal `source_ip`, optional `user_id`, `drop` and/or `block_seconds`. Omit `user_id` for an agent-wide IP action; supply it for that user's sessions. `drop: true` closes matching current sessions. A temporary block of 1?604800 seconds rejects future admission until its durable deadline; combining both closes current sessions and prevents immediate reconnection.

`unblock: true` removes the matching temporary IP restriction. It cannot be combined with `block_seconds`; it may accompany a drop. User/IP blocks match the canonical address, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 normalization. They are admission controls rather than a new host firewall ruleset.

## Explain blocked admission
`telemetry.report` includes a per-user admission status in `users.status[userID]` with an explicit `limited` boolean, a reason when restricted, and a `scope` of `new_connection` or `new_ip`. Reaching an active-IP quota restricts additional source IPs; already active source addresses remain eligible when other quotas permit. `admission.rejected` reports an attempted rejection with `user_id`, `limited: true` and a machine-readable `reason`. Its source IP is included only when recurring IP reporting has been requested.

Rejection reasons are `block_new`, `ip_temp_block`, `torrent_ban`, `active_ip_limit`, `connection_limit`, `blocked_port`, `ineligible` and `storage_backpressure`. A user-wide status describes restrictions known from the current snapshot; an IP-specific decision also depends on the attempted source IP.

## Revocation and cleanup
Credential rotation removes old authorization before new credentials are installed. Removing a user or inbound eligibility closes existing affected sessions. Reservations are released exactly once on failure, closure or UDP expiry. Session lists are snapshots: a returned session may close before a later control request.

guides.title: Traffic & telemetry
guides.description: Idempotent billing, online snapshots and bounded observability.
guides.body:
## Durable billing batches
`traffic.report` contains a stable batch `id` and a `traffic` map. Each key is a user ID and its value is `[upload_bytes, download_bytes]`, measured in bytes. Journal persistence happens before transmission. A restart or reconnect may replay the same batch.

Persist the deduplication ID and bill the batch atomically in the master, then send `traffic.ack` with the batch ID in `data.id`. Never acknowledge before durable acceptance. Duplicate reports must be acknowledged again without charging twice. Only the matching pending batch is retired by the agent.

## Backpressure
The journal has a storage bound and explicit backpressure. Storage exhaustion cannot silently discard traffic. Observe readiness and rejection reasons; address storage or acknowledgement failures before asking the agent to resume normal work.

## Current online state
`telemetry.report` is an authoritative current snapshot. Replace the master's current online set instead of merging indefinitely. A user missing from active connection counts has zero active sessions. IP details are omitted unless requested. A fresh `boot_id` distinguishes counter generations after restart.

Track `connected`, `liveness`, `ready`, `synchronized`, envelope `revision` and `config_revision` separately. Machine metrics and certificate status are snapshots; they do not require a traffic acknowledgement.

## Logs and measurements
One shared sampler produces immutable machine metrics. The default sample interval is one second and reporting interval is five seconds. Throughput uses actual elapsed time. CPU, memory, swap, disks, interfaces, process/connection counts, uptime, virtualization and available GPU collectors are included. Unavailable collectors report status.

`logs.report` carries bounded redacted entries and the number dropped from the log queue. Rejection and transport-drop counters help distinguish an idle user from a restricted or overloaded agent.

configuration_intro:
## Configuration authority
Operational settings arrive inside `state.sync` or `config.apply`; the local bootstrap contains only the master connection URL and token. `xray` and `users` are required, including `users: []` when every account should be removed.

The tables below are generated directly from the tracked JSON Schema. Runtime validation also checks native Xray configuration, unique IDs/tags, provider references, port ranges and other semantic constraints. [Download configuration schema](downloads/schemas/config.schema.json).

## Top-level fields
downloads_intro:
## Machine-readable contracts
[Download OpenAPI 3.1](downloads/openapi.json) · [Download AsyncAPI 3.1](downloads/asyncapi.json) · [Master message JSON Schema](downloads/schemas/master-message.schema.json) · [Remote configuration JSON Schema](downloads/schemas/config.schema.json)

OpenAPI describes the actual authenticated WebSocket upgrade. Operations after upgrade are application frames, documented through the accompanying schemas and AsyncAPI. Relative schema references resolve against the downloaded `schemas/` directory.

## Source documentation
[Protocol Markdown](downloads/docs/protocol.md) · [Native capability inventory](downloads/docs/features.md) · [Migration guide](downloads/docs/migration.md) · [Release notes](downloads/docs/release-notes.md)

These files are copied from the repository when the site is built. The site uses no external documentation renderer or runtime CDN.

fields.xray: Native root Xray configuration. Tagged inbounds and native outbounds, routing, transports and resolver settings are retained; managed accounts and accounting are generated separately.
fields.users: Authoritative user set. Empty removes all authorization; missing/null is invalid.
fields.providers: Named DNS-provider configurations and credentials used by certificate profiles and DDNS jobs. Treat every credential as secret.
fields.certificates: Named certificate profiles shared by inbounds. Reusing a profile shares its certificate manager.
fields.inbound_certificates: Map of inbound tag to named certificate profile.
fields.ddns: Managed A/AAAA jobs. Only each job's configured records are modified.
fields.dns: Resolver mode and optional guarded port-53 redirection. Xray DNS is the default.
fields.firewall: Complete host nftables policy with protected SSH access and independent rollback confirmation.
fields.blocked_ports: Outbound destination-port ranges enforced before dispatch; matching established flows close after policy changes.
fields.asset_hashes: Map of managed Geodata filename to expected SHA-256 digest. Verified files are staged atomically.
fields.telemetry: Sampler/report cadence and opt-in recurring source-IP reporting.
fields.torrent: BitTorrent detection and temporary user admission block policy.
fields.updates: Stable release policy. Daily checks run; automatic installation is disabled by default.
fields.users.id: Positive user ID assigned by the master; unique inside a snapshot.
fields.users.uuid: Default protocol account UUID when a per-inbound native credential is not supplied.
fields.users.credentials: Map of eligible inbound tag to native account object. The agent manages email and level identity fields.
fields.users.inbound_tags: Unique eligible managed inbound tags. At least one is required.
fields.users.active_ip_limit: Distinct active source-IP limit across inbounds. Zero means unlimited.
fields.users.connection_limit: Logical active TCP/UDP stream limit across inbounds. Zero means unlimited.
fields.users.speed_limit_mbps: Normal aggregate upload plus download rate in Mbps. Zero with no burst ceiling disables throttling.
fields.users.block_new: Reject newly admitted streams while retaining eligible established streams.
fields.telemetry.sample_seconds: Sample interval, default 1 second. Zero selects the default.
fields.telemetry.report_seconds: Report interval, default 5 seconds. Zero selects the default.
fields.telemetry.include_active_ips: Explicit request to include user-associated active IPs in recurring reports; default false.
fields.torrent.enabled: Enable classified BitTorrent detection, flow blocking and temporary user bans.
fields.torrent.ban_seconds: Ban duration, default 600 seconds (10 minutes). Zero selects the default.
fields.updates.enabled: Permit policy-driven automatic stable release installation. Default false.
fields.dns.redirect: Redirect port 53 only after the selected loopback resolver is ready for TCP and UDP.
fields.dns.upstreams: SmartDNS DNS-over-TLS endpoints using tls://host[:port]; required for SmartDNS mode.
fields.providers.credentials: Provider-specific credential map delivered securely over WSS.
fields.certificates.provider: Named provider for certificate DNS challenge operations.
fields.certificates.config: Certificate source and ACME configuration; secret key material is redacted from reports.
fields.certificates.config.cert_mode: Certificate mode supported by the manager: provided files/content or automatic issuance.
fields.certificates.config.dns_provider: DNS provider name for DNS-01 issuance.
fields.certificates.config.dns_env: Provider environment values used by the certificate manager; secret.
fields.certificates.config.http_port: Challenge listener port when the selected issuance mode uses HTTP.
fields.certificates.config.auto_tls: Automatic TLS behavior of the certificate profile.
fields.ddns.id: Unique DDNS job identifier, used by ddns.run.
fields.ddns.zone: DNS zone managed by the selected provider.
fields.ddns.name: Record name whose A and/or AAAA records this job owns.
fields.ddns.ipv4: Explicit IPv4 address when not discovered dynamically.
fields.ddns.ipv6: Explicit IPv6 address when not discovered dynamically.
fields.ddns.interface: Interface used for local address discovery.
fields.firewall.enabled: Enable agent ownership of the host ruleset.
fields.firewall.protect: Enable probe protection and temporary source-prefix bans.
fields.firewall.ssh_ports: SSH management ports retained during every transaction.
fields.firewall.allow_prefixes: IP/CIDR allowlist preserved in the generated policy.
fields.firewall.forward: Typed TCP/UDP forwarding rules with explicit destination addresses and ports.
fields.blocked_ports.from: First destination port in the inclusive blocked range (1–65535).
fields.blocked_ports.to: Last destination port in the inclusive blocked range; at least from.
fields.blocked_ports.network: tcp or udp; omitted applies to both.
fields.users.burst_speed_limit_mbps: Always enforced burst ceiling in Mbps, at least the normal rate. Omission keeps the fixed normal cap.
fields.users.speed_limit_after_seconds: Consecutive seconds above normal before applying the normal cap; default 10.
fields.users.speed_limit_reset_seconds: Seconds below 90% of normal before allowing bursts again; default 1.
fields.users.accounting_period: Master-owned accounting period ID, never reused. Requires traffic_periods_v1.
fields.users.valid_until: RFC3339 deadline enforced from cached state while disconnected. Requires authorization_expiry.
fields.member_outbounds: Generated member proxy tags whose literal public endpoints and owned dependencies are verified on the agent.

messages.name: agent.hello
messages.description: Identify the durable agent and current process before synchronization.
messages.body:
## First frame
Sent before other application frames on every new socket. The payload identifies the persisted agent, a fresh process boot ID, agent/core versions, applied revision and supported capabilities. Use durable identity for enrollment and billing; use the boot ID to recognize a new process/counter generation.

## Next step
Wait for `state.request`, then send an authoritative snapshot. A hello reports current state; it does not authorize the master to skip synchronization.

## Optional master capabilities
Negotiate traffic_periods_v1, measured_user_rates, authorization_expiry and member_outbound_guards. upgrade_pending delays first adoption until binary rollback confirmation.

messages.name: state.request
messages.description: Request a full authoritative state after connect or synchronization loss.
messages.body:
## When emitted
The agent sends this after hello and after reconnect, a revision gap or receive-buffer overflow. Return a complete `state.sync` using the authoritative current revision. Cached operation continues during an outage; the master still needs to resynchronize when the socket returns.

messages.name: state.sync
messages.description: Establish a complete native runtime and user authorization baseline.
messages.body:
## Authoritative state
Supply a complete remote configuration. Both `xray` and `users` are required. An explicit empty user array removes every user. Missing/null users produce a validation error.

Use a monotonic revision. An identical successfully applied snapshot at the same revision is acknowledged without reapplication. Correct failures with a higher revision. Observe accepted and applied separately. [Configuration fields](#/configuration).

messages.name: config.apply
messages.description: Replace the complete accepted configuration with an exact base revision.
messages.body:
## Replace configuration
Send the full remote configuration, a new monotonic `revision` and the exact current `base_revision`. Omitted settings are replaced by their defaults. The agent validates before changing listeners. Authorization revocation remains effective if runtime activation fails.

Use `state.sync` to recover from a base mismatch. [Configuration fields](#/configuration).

messages.name: users.sync
messages.description: Replace the entire authorized user set without replacing native configuration.
messages.body:
## Replace authorization
`users` is an explicit required array. `[]` revokes every account. Credentials and eligible inbound tags are validated. Removed users and changed credentials close affected existing sessions. New credentials are installed after revocation.

Supply a new `revision` and current `base_revision`.

fields.users: Complete user list; empty is authoritative removal.

messages.name: users.delta
messages.description: Add, replace and remove users against a known authorization revision.
messages.body:
## Apply a delta
`upsert` supplies full user replacements; `remove` supplies positive user IDs to revoke. A credential change or removed eligibility revokes affected sessions before new authorization is installed.

Supply a new `revision` and exact current `base_revision`. A missing base or gap triggers a full state request.

fields.upsert: Complete user objects to insert or replace.
fields.remove: User IDs to remove from authorization.

messages.name: user.controls
messages.description: Set per-user block_new decisions while retaining eligible existing streams.
messages.body:
## Admission control
Each item contains a positive user `id` and a `block_new` boolean. True rejects new streams; false removes this master-imposed restriction. Existing eligible streams remain open. Other restrictions, such as a temporary ban or reached quota, still apply.

This is a revisioned mutation with exact `base_revision`. Connection-derived controls remain in memory across reconnects during this process lifetime. Restart clears them; the master recomputes controls from fresh available reports. The agent advertises `volatile_connection_controls_v1` and removes previously persisted controls on upgrade.

fields.users: User IDs and explicit block_new decisions.

messages.name: state.accepted
messages.description: Acknowledge durable acceptance of authorization and configuration intent.
messages.body:
## Persistence acknowledgement
The requested authorization has been persisted under private state. The accepted revision is now authoritative for subsequent deltas. Runtime activation can still be pending. Do not interpret acceptance as proof that new listeners are serving.

Wait for `state.applied` or `state.failed` and observe telemetry readiness.

messages.name: state.applied
messages.description: Acknowledge activation of the requested runtime revision.
messages.body:
## Runtime activation
The proxy runtime has successfully activated the requested revision. Correlate the envelope ID and revision with the original mutation. Telemetry readiness and configuration revision provide the continuing current state.

messages.name: state.failed
messages.description: Report a runtime activation error while preserving authoritative revocation.
messages.body:
## Activation failure
The accepted authorization revision remains durable even when runtime replacement fails. A rollback cannot restore removed users or rotated credentials. The error is safe to display without raw credentials. Send corrected configuration with a higher revision and monitor runtime readiness.

messages.name: telemetry.report
messages.description: Report runtime state, user admission status and immutable host metrics.
messages.body:
## Current snapshot
The payload includes `agent_id`, `boot_id`, `time`, `connected`, `liveness`, `ready`, `synchronized`, `config_revision`, `users`, `machine`, `certificates` and transport-drop information. Envelope `revision` tracks accepted authorization.

## Users and privacy
Replace the master's current online connection set. Missing active users mean zero sessions. `users.status[userID]` supplies `user_id`, `limited: true/false`, a reason when blocked and `scope` (`new_connection` or `new_ip`). `users.connections` contains current counts and `users.active_ips` is present only when requested. IP/destination-specific restrictions are reported for attempted admissions; they do not claim that every new user stream is blocked. Source IPs are omitted by default. `telemetry.include_active_ips: true` explicitly requests user-associated active IPs in recurring snapshots. An explicit `users.active_ips` query obtains one-time details.

## Delivery
The default report interval is five seconds. This is a disposable snapshot and needs no acknowledgement. Durable billing uses traffic.report instead.

## Measured speed
users.rates reports upload_bytes_per_second, download_bytes_per_second and sample_seconds. These measured byte rates are independent of users.speed decimal Mbps limits.

messages.name: traffic.report
messages.description: Replay-safe upload/download byte batches for durable billing.
messages.body:
## Bill exactly once
The payload contains a stable `id` and `traffic`, a map of user IDs to `[upload_bytes, download_bytes]`. The journal is written before transmission. A replay after retry or restart uses the same ID.

Atomically deduplicate and bill in the master, then send `traffic.ack`. Duplicate receipt should also be acknowledged, without billing again. Only the matching pending batch is retired.

## Period accounting
With traffic_periods_v1, samples contain user_id, accounting_period, from/through timestamps and exact upload_bytes/download_bytes. Bill samples rather than adding legacy traffic again. Sealed batches and old accounting periods survive replay and restart.

messages.name: traffic.ack
messages.description: Retire a matching batch after durable master-side acceptance.
messages.body:
## Acknowledge durable receipt
Put the exact traffic batch ID in `data.id`. Acknowledgements for a different pending batch never retire the current one. Send only after your deduplication and billing transaction commits.

If acknowledgement delivery is uncertain, acknowledge the replayed report again.

fields.id: Stable traffic.report batch ID already durably processed by the master.

messages.name: logs.report
messages.description: Stream bounded, redacted log entries and dropped-entry counts.
messages.body:
## Log snapshot
`entries` contains timestamped agent/core messages. `dropped` counts entries lost from the bounded queue. Tokens, account credentials and private certificate material are redacted before serialization. Do not use logs as an authoritative billing or state channel. No acknowledgement is required.

messages.name: admission.rejected
messages.description: Explain why an attempted new user connection was denied.
messages.body:
## Rejection event
Reports the `user_id`, `limited: true` and a machine-readable `reason` when a new authenticated stream is denied. The source IP is included only when recurring IP reporting has been requested.

Reasons identify the actual restriction, such as a master block, temporary ban, active-IP/connection quota, blocked destination or accounting backpressure. Rejection counters also appear in telemetry; an event stream is bounded and should not be used as billing data.

## Fields
| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `user_id` | Numeric authenticated user identity |
| `limited` | Always `true` for a rejected admission |
| `reason` | `storage_backpressure`, `ineligible`, `block_new`, `torrent_ban`, `ip_temp_block`, `blocked_port`, `connection_limit` or `active_ip_limit` |
| `scope` | `new_ip` for an active-IP quota, otherwise `new_connection` |
| `source_ip` | Included only when recurring IP reporting is requested |

messages.name: command
messages.description: Submit one typed remotely managed utility operation.
messages.body:
## Request structure
The envelope `id` is required for command correlation and deduplication. `data.name` selects a supported command and `data.args` is its typed argument object. An omitted args object defaults to `{}`. Unknown commands or malformed arguments fail validation.

Expect accepted, optional progress and a final result. [Command lifecycle](#/command-lifecycle).

messages.name: command.accepted
messages.description: Confirm that a command entered the bounded utility job queue.
messages.body:
## Job acceptance
Correlate the request ID with the submitted command. Acceptance indicates queued work, not successful completion. Two workers execute utility jobs. Retried retained IDs return the existing retained result rather than repeating the operation.

messages.name: command.progress
messages.description: Report an intermediate stage of a long-running utility operation.
messages.body:
## Intermediate progress
Progress is command-specific, for example a speedtest stage or update download/verification stage. Match the operation ID. It is optional and disposable; a final `command.result` determines completion.

messages.name: command.result
messages.description: Return completion status, data or an error for a utility command.
messages.body:
## Final result
Results contain operation `id`, `command`, `status`, completion time and optional `data` or `error`. The last 128 completed results persist across restart. `jobs.list` exposes retained operations.

Some commands, including runtime reconstruction, report queueing or preparation success. Observe runtime state and readiness for actual activation. Mutation results remain authoritative when a subsequent cancellation arrives.

messages.name: command.cancel
messages.description: Cancel a queued or running operation by its original command ID.
messages.body:
## Cooperative cancellation
`data.id` names the original operation. Cancellation propagates to context-aware transfers and providers. It cannot reverse a mutation already committed by an external provider or host operation. Inspect retained results before retrying.

fields.id: Original command request ID to cancel.

messages.name: error
messages.description: Report invalid frames, unsupported requests or stale revisions.
messages.body:
## Protocol error
Correlate the envelope ID when present. Invalid shapes, unsupported message types and stale revisions produce a sanitized error. A synchronization gap also triggers `state.request`; send a full authoritative snapshot. Never send credentials or raw master messages to logs while diagnosing an error.

messages.name: firewall.pending
messages.description: Announce an unconfirmed firewall transaction protected by rollback.
messages.body:
## Connectivity confirmation
The live ruleset is applied with an independent watchdog. The master must test that it can communicate with the agent over the existing or re-established socket, then issue `firewall.confirm` using the transaction ID.

Transactions default to 45 seconds. Missing confirmation restores both prior live rules and persisted policy. Keep configured SSH management ports available.

messages.name: torrent.detected
messages.description: Report detected BitTorrent traffic and its user ban deadline.
messages.body:
## Temporary user restriction
When torrent policy is enabled, a classified flow is blocked, that user's sessions close and new sessions are rejected for the configured ban. The default is ten minutes. The event reports `user_id` and a deadline. Ban expiry is durable across restart.

A master `block_new` decision remains independent of torrent expiry.

messages.name: torrent.expired
messages.description: Report expiry of a durable temporary torrent ban.
messages.body:
## Ban expiry
The torrent restriction has expired for the reported user. Other restrictions such as master `block_new`, IP bans and quotas still apply. Read the current admission status before treating a user as unrestricted.

messages.name: firewall.events
messages.description: Durable report-only detections and ban lifecycle events.
messages.body: Threshold reports contain stable event IDs, detection time, IP, rule and count. Persist before acknowledging. Detection never authorizes a new ban. Expiry events identify the authoritative generation; wait for all participating nodes before global removal.

messages.name: firewall.events.ack
messages.description: Acknowledge durably processed firewall events.
messages.body: Send event IDs only after committing their effects. The agent replays unacknowledged events after reconnect. Acknowledging an obsolete generation cannot remove a newer ban.

commands.name: connections.list
commands.description: Inspect a bounded page of authenticated logical sessions.
commands.body:
## Session details
Returns current session records with user identity, source IP, inbound tag and destination metadata. This explicit query requests connection detail; it is separate from recurring IP-reporting policy.

## Pagination
Pass `after` as the last returned session ID. Sessions are sorted by ID. This is a live snapshot, so entries may close between requests. The default page size is 100; the maximum supported size is 1000.

commands.name: connections.close
commands.description: Close one session or a user's matching inbound sessions.
commands.body:
## Targeted closure
Choose either a session `id` or a positive `user_id` with optional `inbound_tag`. Closing releases admission slots exactly once. User-wide closure returns an acknowledgement even when no current sessions match; a single session closure reports whether it was found.

Dropping a session alone permits reconnection when current policy allows it. Use ips.control to combine an IP drop with a temporary admission block.
fields: Positive user ID; when set, selects the user's sessions.
Narrow user-session closure to one inbound.

commands.name: users.active_ips
commands.description: Request current active source IPs associated with user IDs.
commands.body:
## Explicit IP request
Returns active user/IP observations on demand. Source IPs are associated with positive user IDs and reflect established logical sessions. A user with no active sessions has no active source addresses.

Supply `user_id` to narrow the query, or omit it to inspect all current users. This command does not turn on recurring IP reporting. Configure `telemetry.include_active_ips` separately if recurring observations are required.

## Result data
The result is an array of `{user_id, source_ip, connections}` observations, sorted by user ID and source address. `connections` counts active logical sessions from that address. An empty array means no matching active source IPs.

```json
[{"user_id":7,"source_ip":"203.0.113.25","connections":2}]
```
fields: Positive user ID; omitted queries current users.

commands.name: ips.control
commands.description: Drop and/or temporarily block a specific source IP.
commands.body:
## Scope and action
A literal `source_ip` is required. `user_id` narrows the action to one user's sessions; omitted or zero applies agent-wide. At least one action is required: `drop: true`, `block_seconds` from 1 to 604800, or `unblock: true`. `unblock` cannot be combined with `block_seconds`.

Dropping closes current matches. A temporary block prevents matching new streams until its persisted deadline. `unblock: true` clears that exact user/IP block without removing other restrictions. Combining them prevents immediate reconnection. Address normalization includes IPv4-mapped IPv6. This command uses the agent admission registry; it does not replace the host firewall policy.

## Result
The final result reports the applied action and temporary deadline where applicable. The current telemetry/rejection reason explains subsequent admission restrictions.
fields: Literal IPv4 or IPv6 address to match.
Positive user ID; omitted or zero means agent-wide.
Clear the matching temporary IP block; incompatible with block_seconds.

commands.name: metrics.get
commands.description: Read the latest immutable machine sample.
commands.body:
## Metrics snapshot
Returns the shared sampler's current host, CPU, memory, swap, disk, interface, connection/process count, uptime, virtualization and runtime metrics. Available NVIDIA/AMD collectors are included; missing collectors expose unavailable status. Does not start a second sampler.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: certificates.get
commands.description: Inspect certificate readiness, expiry and renewal status.
commands.body:
## Certificate status
Returns named profile status from shared certificate managers. Inbounds referencing the same profile reuse issuance and renewal work. Private keys and provider credentials are excluded.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: jobs.list
commands.description: Inspect current and retained utility job results.
commands.body:
## Retained operations
Returns the agent's bounded job view, including statuses and retained completion results. The last 128 completed operations persist across restart. Use the original request ID to correlate commands and assess uncertain outcomes before retrying.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: runtime.reload
commands.description: Recheck external material and incrementally apply current desired state.
commands.body:
## Incremental reload
Requires incremental_reload_v1 and activation_commands_v1. Rechecks certificate and asset material and applies the prepared candidate through the existing incremental runtime. Unchanged listeners and sessions remain running. Immutable core changes reconstruct after successful preparation.

## Forced recovery
Set force to true to explicitly reconstruct. Completion follows activation and readiness; a newer desired configuration supersedes this request without blocking traffic acknowledgments.
fields: Force full recovery reconstruction. Default false.

commands.name: ddns.run
commands.description: Run one accepted DDNS job immediately.
commands.body:
## Managed records
`job_id` must identify a job in the accepted remote configuration. The command uses that job's named DNS provider and only modifies its configured A/AAAA records. Unknown jobs fail. Provider errors remain visible in the result. Cancellation cannot undo an already accepted provider mutation.

commands.name: geodata.refresh
commands.description: Refresh verified assets and queue a new runtime generation.
commands.body:
## Verified generations
Uses native Geodata asset/cron/outbound settings and remotely supplied hashes. Filenames stay in the managed directory. Files are staged, verified and replaced atomically as a generation. Required failure retains the previous valid files.

Successful refresh queues incremental application; immutable core changes reconstruct only when required. Observe readiness for activation. The core's duplicate downloader is suppressed.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: firewall.status
commands.description: Read current host policy and pending transaction status.
commands.body:
## Host firewall status
Returns managed nftables state and pending confirmation details. Use this to identify an unconfirmed transaction before issuing firewall.confirm. Host ruleset ownership is complete, including persisted nftables policy.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: firewall.apply
commands.description: Atomically install a validated host ruleset with rollback protection.
commands.body:
## Complete host policy
`policy` supplies the typed remote firewall structure. Allowed services, SSH ports, IP prefixes, protection and TCP/UDP forwarding are rendered into one validated candidate. There is no conntrack connection quota.

Optional DNS redirection is accepted only after loopback resolver readiness. A pending transaction is guarded by an independent systemd watchdog. Test master connectivity, then confirm its transaction ID before the default 45-second deadline. Missing confirmation restores live rules and persisted policy.
fields: Complete FirewallPolicy; see remote configuration fields.
Guarded port-53 redirection after resolver readiness.

commands.name: firewall.confirm
commands.description: Confirm connectivity for a specific pending firewall transaction.
commands.body:
## Commit after connectivity testing
Use the transaction ID from firewall.pending or the apply result. Confirm through the existing or re-established control socket only after testing that the master can still reach the agent. A different or expired transaction ID fails. Successful confirmation cancels the rollback watchdog.

commands.name: speedtest
commands.description: Measure latency and throughput through a peer using isolated Xray.
commands.body:
## Peer test
Supply native `peer_outbound` credentials/settings and HTTPS upload/download endpoints controlled by the master. The agent uses an isolated outbound-only Xray client, never the managed inbound runtime. It reports connection/request latency and transfer throughput with cleanup and cancellation.

## Bounds
Default latency sampling is three requests. Default transfers are bounded to 32 MiB download and 8 MiB upload within 60 seconds total. `max_bytes` may reach 64 MiB and `timeout_seconds` may reach 120. Endpoints must accept the intended test payloads.
fields: Native Xray outbound object for the target peer.
Transfer bound in bytes; maximum 64 MiB.

commands.name: update.check
commands.description: Check the selected stable release and authenticated artifact metadata.
commands.body:
## Stable release discovery
Returns update availability for the current platform and policy. Checks also run daily. This command does not install a binary. Artifacts must have a SHA-256 manifest authenticated by the pinned Minisign production public key.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: update.install
commands.description: Install a signed stable binary with rollback-aware lifecycle handling.
commands.body:
## Verified installation
Optional `version` selects a stable release. The agent verifies the manifest signature and binary hash before execution. Protected signing secrets belong to release infrastructure. Test signing keys never enter production trust roots.

Observe progress/result and process reconnect/readiness. Retain the generated identity and pending traffic state through replacement.
fields: Stable release version; otherwise use selected/latest stable policy.

commands.name: update.rollback
commands.description: Restore the retained prior binary without deleting durable state.
commands.body:
## Prior release
Restores the retained previous binary when rollback is available. Reconnect and readiness confirm the restarted agent's behavior. Preserve the state directory, identity, accepted restrictions and pending traffic.

## Arguments
Use an empty object.

commands.name: traffic.flush
commands.description: Seal captured traffic and obtain a durable accounting cutoff.
commands.body:
## Accounting barrier
The optional user_id selects the user to quiesce; omission selects all users. Set quiesce only after new admission has been blocked. The agent waits for native handlers and their final payload bytes, then seals traffic without replacing an outstanding batch.

The result contains agent_id, sequence, through and quiesced. Commit all reports through that sequence before resetting or settling the old accounting period. A command result by itself does not prove the master has ingested the reports.

## Renewal continuity
Specify accounting_period to wait only for a revoked old period. The current new period remains admitted. The barrier echoes the requested accounting period.
fields: Positive user ID; zero or omission selects every user.
Close fenced sessions and wait for native completion before sealing.
With quiesce and a positive user ID, finish only this old period while renewed streams remain active. Requires traffic_period_barriers_v1.

commands.name: config.validate
commands.description: Validate a complete native configuration without starting listeners.
commands.body:
## Node preflight
Send the remote configuration directly as args, including users. The agent validates protocol policy, managed accounts, native fields, and node-local assets using its pinned core. No listener starts and no configuration becomes authoritative. Requires config_validation_v1. Command arguments and results remain memory-only.
fields: Managed accounts; an empty array revokes every account in the candidate.

commands.name: firewall.bans.get
commands.description: Read live firewall enforcement metadata.
commands.body: Returns versions, source generations and bounded pending-report counts. This live result is excluded from retained command history.

commands.name: firewall.bans.sync
commands.description: Stage an authoritative bounded snapshot.
commands.body: Ordered chunks publish only on the final chunk. SourcesOnly snapshots have an independent version bank and never replace dynamic bans or exact exemptions. Source references reuse a cached matching generation without transmitting CIDRs again.

commands.name: firewall.bans.update
commands.description: Apply an authoritative ban or exact exemption delta.
commands.body: Absolute deadlines replace prior durations, including shortening. Stable generation and version make retries idempotent. Remove and RemoveExemptions apply immediate unban/revocation without restarting Xray.

commands.name: update.status
commands.description: Inspect the durable upgrade transaction without waiting for utility capacity.
commands.body:
## Recovery inspection
Returns transaction id, version, previous, status and deadline, or idle before any transaction. Match install results by request ID. After reconnect require confirmed transaction status and fresh ready/synchronized telemetry at the current revision. Capability: update_transaction_v1. This read and jobs.list can reply directly with command.result.

commands.name: firewall.geoip.sync
commands.description: Stage a bounded disk-backed country IP generation.
commands.body:
## Country range staging
Requires source_geoip_stream_v1. Probe a generation before uploading. Chunks carry generation, index and at most 256 prefixes; final publishes the immutable file. Activate with SourceGeoIPPolicy reference. Staging cannot replace current enforcement until publication.

commands.name: firewall.protected.sync
commands.description: Replace volatile trusted managed-node address exclusions.
commands.body:
## Managed-node protection
Requires firewall_master_observation_v1. Accepts at most 100000 exact canonical public IPs from trusted node address information. The agent combines this snapshot with its own observed interface addresses and active member whitelist protection. The snapshot remains memory-only and is replaced on reconciliation. Shared CDN ranges are never inferred from subscription hostnames.
